V.}}</noinclude>For vvhat things {{ls}}oeuer he doeth, the{{ls}}e the Sonne al{{ls}}o doeth in like maner. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=20}}† For the Father loueth the Sonne, and {{ls}}hevveth him al things that him {{ls}}elf doeth, and greater vvorkes then the{{ls}}e vvil he {{ls}}hevv him, that you may marueil. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=21}}† For as the Father doth rai{{ls}}e the dead and quickeneth: {{ls}}o the Sonne al{{ls}}o quickeneth vvhom he vvil. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=22}}† For neither doth the Father iudge any man: but al iudgement he hath giuen to the Sonne, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=23}}† that al may honour the Sonne, as they doe honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Sonne, doth not honour the Father, vvho {{ls}}ent him. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=24}}† Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, that he vvhich heareth my vvord, and beleeueth him that {{ls}}ent me, hath life euerla{{ls}}ting. and he commeth not into iudgement, but {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`is pa{{ls}}{{ls}}ed.''}}`{{ls}}hal pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e' from death into life. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=25}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō Al{{ls}}oules day.}}Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, that the houre commeth, and novv it is, vvhen the dead {{ls}}hal heare the voice of the Sonne of God, and they that haue heard, {{ls}}hal liue. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=26}}† For as the Father hath life in him {{ls}}elf: {{ls}}o he hath giuen to the Sonne al{{ls}}o to haue life in him {{ls}}elf: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=27}}† and he hath giuen him povver to doe iudgement al{{ls}}o, becau{{ls}}e he is the Sonne of man. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=28}}† Marueil not at this, becau{{ls}}e the houre commeth vvherein al that are in the graues, {{ls}}hal heare his voice, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=29}}† and they that haue {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not faith only, but good and il deedes {{ls}}hal be counted, and accordingly rewarded at the day of iudgement.}}∷ done good things, {{ls}}hal come forth into the re{{ls}}urrection of life: but they that haue done euil, into the re{{ls}}urrection of iudgement.⊣ {{verse|chapter=5|verse=30}}† I can not of my {{ls}}elf doe any thing. As I heare, {{ls}}o I iudge: and my iudgement is iu{{ls}}t. becau{{ls}}e I {{ls}}eeke not my vvil, but the vvil of him that {{ls}}ent me. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=31}}† If I giue te{{ls}}timonie of my {{ls}}elf, my te{{ls}}timonie is not true. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=32}}† There is an other that giueth te{{ls}}timonie of me: and I knovv that the te{{ls}}timonie is true vvhich he giueth of me.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=33}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 1, 19.''}}* You {{ls}}ent to Iohn: and he gaue te{{ls}}timonie to the truth.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=34}}† But {{sup|‖}} I receiue not te{{ls}}timonie of man: but I {{ls}}ay the{{ls}}e things that you may be {{ls}}aued. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=35}}† He vvas the lampe burning and {{ls}}hining. And you vvould for a time reioyce in his light. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=36}}† But I haue a greater te{{ls}}timonie then Iohn. For the vvorkes vvhich the Father hath giuen me to perfit them: the very vvorkes them {{ls}}elues vvhich I doe, giue te{{ls}}timonie of me, that the Father hath {{ls}}ent me. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=37}}† And the Father that {{ls}}ent me, him {{ls}}elf hath {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 3, 17.''}}* giuen te{{ls}}timonie of me. neither haue you heard his voice at any time, nor {{ls}}een his {{ls}}hape, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=38}}† and his vvord you haue not remaining in you: becau{{ls}}e vvhom he hath {{ls}}ent, him you beleeue not. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=39}}† {{sup|‖}} Search the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Catholikes {{ls}}earche the {{ls}}criptures, and finde there, Peters & his {{ls}}ucce{{ls}}sors Primacie, the real pre{{ls}}ence, the Prie{{ls}}ts power to forgiue {{ls}}innes, iu{{ls}}tification by faith & good workes, Virginitie preferred before matrimonie, breach of the vow of cōtinencie damnable, voluntarie pouertie, Penāce, almes, and good deedes meritorious, diuers rewardes ĩ heauē accordĩg to diuers merites, & {{ls}}uch like.}}∷ {{ls}}criptures, for you<noinclude>{{rh|||thinke}}</noinclude>
